scope.summary: Implement the engine-agnostic physics-config sidecar per Section 13.18 (BK-18.4, TAI-BK-070), closing GREQ-024: a JSON sidecar accompanying every rigged body with per-region stiffness/damping/gravity/limit parameters keyed by jiggle chain, plus a per-component budget lint (chain count, bones per chain) so game-lane exports stay inside target budgets; engine-specific translations (UE physics asset, Unity/VRM spring bones) are generated FROM this sidecar in 13.26, never hand-authored per engine.
acceptance_criteria: PhysicsSidecar serializes to a documented, versioned JSON schema: { schema_version, skeleton_version, chains: [{ chain_id, region, bones, stiffness, damping, gravity_response, limits }], budgets } — engine-agnostic (no UE/Unity-specific keys; negative test greps for engine terms).
build_sidecar(body_id) assembles the sidecar from the MT-525 generated chains and their derived params; output is deterministic for identical body state.
Budget lint: per-profile budget rules (max chains, max bones per chain, max total secondary bones) evaluate to typed findings; an over-budget fixture fails the lint with the offending chains named.
The sidecar persists as a body-linked artifact via guarded storage and is emitted in the tailor.body event stream on regeneration.
A JSON-schema document for the sidecar format ships alongside the type (schemars-generated) so external engine translators are contract-bound.
scope.risk_if_missed: Hand-tuned per-engine physics configs drift immediately and silently (the Daz-to-UE spring-bone gap); without the sidecar contract plus budget lint, game exports either lose all jiggle motion or blow engine performance budgets with unbounded bone chains.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit skeleton and rigging

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
